subject: Operational ownership & product gating for private subnet pilot
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Elara Chang <elara@hedgehoghealth.com>
Cc: procurement@hedgehoghealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational ownership & product gating for private subnet pilot

Team / Elara —

Quick sync note following our kickoff: Hedgehog Health wants to run a two-week private subnet (VPC) pilot for inference serving. Before we commit to a start date we need to align on three cross-functional items so we don’t run into scope/ops surprises:

1) Operational ownership: who owns day-2 network ops (Redwood runbook + customer network handoff). We need a named owner for: VPC peering, route maintenance, and outage triage.

2) Product gating: the minimal product features we must ship/enable to support the pilot (e.g., prefix caching enabled, dedicated runtime profile, model pinning, telemetry hooks). Please call out any blockers that would force us into an exception lane.

3) Resourcing & SLA asks: estimated engineering hours for pilot setup, required SRE oncall coverage, and whether we need a short-term dedicated GPU pool.

I’ve attached a first-pass runbook and a short network checklist for Hedgehog to review. Elara — can procurement and your network team confirm the expected lead times (VPC peering and firewall exceptions) so we can slot a pilot window?

Action items I’d like by EOD PT tomorrow:
- Karthik: outline technical prerequisites and high-level hours estimate
- Soojin: ops/handoff checklist + oncall plan
- Jonas: compliance/KMS/audit evidence list
- Elara/procurement: expected procurement timelines and any contracting constraints

Thanks — Priya

Attachments: HA-Runbook-v1.pdf, Network-Checklist.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Elara Chang <elara@hedgehoghealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational ownership & product gating for private subnet pilot

Thanks Priya — quick technical read:

- Feasibility: We can run the pilot in a customer VPC with VPC peering + a small NAT/proxy layer on Redwood side. No code changes required for model runtime; however we need:
  * Network ACLs for 443/8443 between the control plane (if customer wants private control plane) and runtime nodes
  * A decision on whether the control plane is customer-hosted or Redwood-managed in an isolated VPC. Customer-hosted control plane adds ~2–3 engineering days for onboarding and secure key exchange. Redwood-hosted with strict peering reduces onboarding time but requires additional contractual data flow language.

- Hours estimate (rough):
  * Network setup & firewall rule verification: 8–12h (infra engineer + customer network)
  * Runtime config and model pinning: 6–10h (infra + product)
  * Runbook + test validation: 4–6h

- GPU pool: For a two-week pilot we can use a shared dedicated pool if they need consistent latency. If they accept best-effort hosted nodes, no extra reservation required.

Blockers: If Hedgehog requires on-prem (air-gapped) execution we need a separate feasibility path; the attached runbook assumes VPC peering only.

I’ll follow up with a sketch of the network flows and a checklist for the onboarding playbook.

—Karthik

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Elara Chang <elara@hedgehoghealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational ownership & product gating for private subnet pilot

Adding operations perspective:

- Handoff & day-2: We need a named Runbook owner on the customer side and an oncall roster from Redwood for the pilot window. Minimal oncall coverage = 1 SRE weekday overlap (0800–1800 PT) and on-call pager for critical outages.

- Acceptance criteria (pilot success):
  1) End-to-end request latency within agreed SLO for 95th percentile
  2) Logs and traces available in our tracing pipeline (no gaps for pilot traffic)
  3) No more than 2 failed restart events related to networking/config in pilot window

- Staffing ask: I recommend we allocate a 0.5 FTE infra engineer for the pilot week + 0.2 FTE product PM for orchestration. If procurement approves a short dedicated pool, SRE load reduces.

I uploaded an ops checklist to the drive (link below) — it includes live-test scripts we should run during validation. Priya — for the named owners, can you confirm who from Hedgehog will own firewall change requests?

Quote: "On Tue, 10 Jul 2028 at 09:12, Priya Natarajan wrote:
> Elara — can procurement and your network team confirm the expected lead times (VPC peering and firewall exceptions) so we can slot a pilot window?"

— Soojin

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Elara Chang <elara@hedgehoghealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational ownership & product gating for private subnet pilot

Security/compliance notes:

- Audit & keys: Hedgehog will need to surface their KMS key policy and the account that will hold the audit logs. If we keep the control plane in Redwood, we must provide SOC2 evidence of logging retention and key access controls.

- Data flow language: If control plane traffic crosses Redwood-managed infrastructure, legal will ask for data flow specifics (types of telemetry collected). We should pre-fill that section in the SoW to avoid last-minute redlines.

- Evidence pack: I need the following for the pilot:
  * KMS key owner and contact
  * Expected data retention period (for logs/metrics)
  * Any regulatory constraints (HIPAA mention from Elara?)

I’ve attached a short checklist for minimal compliance evidence. Also looping in Laura who owns enterprise contracts for a quick review of the SoW template.

On procurement: we should ask Hedgehog to start an NDA + SoW draft now; procurement timelines typically add 7–10 business days for enterprise accounts.

Quote: "On Tue, 10 Jul 2028 at 11:03, Karthik Iyer wrote:
> A decision on whether the control plane is customer-hosted or Redwood-managed in an isolated VPC will materially change onboarding time"

— Jonas

From: Elara Chang <elara@hedgehoghealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational ownership & product gating for private subnet pilot

Thanks all — this is helpful. A few quick clarifications from Hedgehog: 

- Procurement: procurement@hedgehoghealth.com is the right intake (cc’d earlier). We can start the NDA/SoW draft today. Our procurement lead (Marta) can review your template; she typically returns edits in 3–5 business days.

- Network: our network team can provision VPC peering within 48–72 hours once we share the CIDR ranges and firewall rules. I confirmed we can open 443 and 8443 for the pilot. Marta will share the named firewall approver.

- Compliance: Hedgehog is HIPAA-adjacent; we will need the minimal SoW language around PHI non-storage (we do not store PHI for this pilot).

Timeline ask: Can Redwood target a start date two weeks from today (week of Jul 24) assuming procurement and network timelines line up? That would give Hedgehog time to slot an internal review.

We’ll attach any procurement templates to the HubSpot record (link below). Priya — can you confirm the estimated FTEs and the control plane decision by EOD Jul 12 so we can line up internal approvals?

Thanks — Elara

Attachment: Pilot-SoW-draft.docx
